title: Carrier gateway

act2.summary: identical repeated rate requests must hit each carrier's native client at most once

solutions.title: One small adapter class per carrier, one registry
solutions.tradeoff: One class per carrier makes act 1's translation problem disappear cleanly - each adapter owns exactly one native shape, and the registry doesn't care which. But 'at most once' has no single owner here: the cache has to be added three times, once per adapter class, and stays three places to keep in sync from here on.

solutions.title: One class, configured per carrier, switching on the shape internally
solutions.tradeoff: The single parametrised class means the cache only has to be written once. But the branch inside lookUp() is still doing the same three-way translation Adapter split into separate files - now one class carries both the translation and the caching decision, and the two are stacked in the same rate() method.

solutions.title: One validating entry point over the whole carrier subsystem
solutions.tradeoff: The cache attaches to the one operation the subsystem exposes, in the one place that operation is defined - the cheapest possible landing spot for a rule about repeated calls. The price was paid earlier: the facade already has to know about all three carriers' shapes inside mappers.ts, which is exactly what Adapter's file-per-carrier split exists to avoid.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
In the adapter route, does the cache truly need to live three times - once per adapter class - or could a reader argue for a shared base class, and at what cost?
Does every route's cache key include carrierId as well as the three request fields, so two different carriers' calls can't collide?
Is 'the operation act 2's rule is about already has exactly one place to live' a fair reading of why facade wins here - and would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have said the same thing?
Do all three routes agree, byte for byte, on what happens in act 1 - same cents, same etaDays, for the same input?
